Fragile items need a different moving process.

Most moving damage happens when fragile items are treated like regular household goods. Our process focuses on preparation, separation, protection, and controlled handling from the first pickup to final placement.

Pre-move review

We identify fragile pieces, oversized items, artwork, glass, antiques, and anything that needs special attention before moving day.

Protection plan

Items may be wrapped, padded, boxed, labeled, separated, or loaded in a safer sequence depending on the move.

Controlled delivery

Fragile items are placed carefully, not rushed into a general unload pile. Placement matters.

Best fit for clients who care about condition, not just speed.

This page is for customers moving delicate, expensive, sentimental, decorative, or hard-to-replace items. If your move includes artwork, fragile décor, glass pieces, antiques, designer furniture, mirrors, or collectibles, it should be planned separately from standard boxes and furniture.

Homes & apartments: fragile décor, mirrors, framed artwork, and delicate furniture.
Offices & showrooms: wall art, glass boards, display items, and reception pieces.
Storage moves: careful inventory flow, labeling, and organized placement.
Packing-only jobs: protection before another carrier or internal team moves the items.

What we can help protect and move

Every item is different. The goal is to reduce handling mistakes, keep fragile pieces separated from heavy items, and make delivery clean and controlled.

Artwork & framed pieces

Canvas art, framed prints, photography, wall art, decorative panels, and gallery-style pieces that require careful surface protection and upright handling.

Mirrors & glass items

Large mirrors, glass tops, glass doors, lamps, shelves, tabletops, display pieces, and items that need extra padding and clear fragile labeling.

Antiques & sentimental items

Older furniture, family pieces, collectibles, fragile décor, and items with high personal value that should not be handled casually.

Designer furniture & delicate finishes

Marble, lacquer, polished wood, light fabric, custom pieces, and furniture where scratches, pressure marks, and edge damage matter.

Packing-only preparation

We can prepare fragile items before a move, renovation, storage transfer, or delivery handled by another party.

Storage coordination

Fragile items can be labeled, separated, and positioned with care for easier access and safer long-term organization.

Our fragile moving process

A safer move is not only about materials. It is about sequence, communication, and crew discipline.

Review

We ask what is fragile, valuable, oversized, framed, glass, antique, or difficult to replace.

Plan

We decide what needs packing, padding, boxing, labeling, disassembly, or separate handling.

Protect

Items are wrapped and prepared based on material, shape, weight, and risk.

Load

Fragile pieces are not buried under heavy furniture or mixed into general loose items.

Place

Delivery is handled with clear placement instructions and careful final positioning.

When to book fragile or artwork moving support

This service is useful when the move includes pieces that are expensive, breakable, sentimental, custom-made, difficult to replace, or sensitive to pressure, scratches, vibration, or poor loading.

  • Apartment moves with mirrors, glass, artwork, and delicate décor
  • House moves with antiques, framed art, lamps, marble, or collectibles
  • Office moves with wall art, glass boards, awards, and display pieces
  • Storage moves where items must be protected and labeled correctly
  • Packing-only support before a renovation, staging, or relocation

Clear communication before the crew arrives.

For the best result, send photos of fragile pieces before the move. We can review size, access, stairs, elevator rules, packing needs, and whether special materials or extra time should be planned.

Helpful photos: front view, side view, close-up of fragile surfaces, and access path.
Helpful details: dimensions, approximate weight, pickup floor, delivery floor, elevator access, and storage requirements.
Important note: some high-value artwork may require specialty crating or third-party insurance. We will be clear if a piece needs a higher level of preparation.

A controlled handling system from first touch to final placement.

Our process is built to reduce risk, prevent confusion, and give clients confidence when moving valuable or fragile items.

Custom Crating & Protection

Fragile & artwork moving FAQs

Common questions before booking a careful moving service.

Do you move artwork?

Yes. We can help move framed art, canvas pieces, wall art, decorative panels, and similar pieces as part of a local move, storage move, or packing-only project.

Can you pack fragile items before the move?

Yes. Packing-only support is available for fragile items, artwork, mirrors, lamps, glass pieces, and delicate décor.

Should I send photos before booking?

Yes. Photos help us understand size, material, access, packing needs, and whether special preparation should be planned.

Do fragile items cost more to move?

Sometimes. Fragile items may require more time, more materials, extra crew attention, or a different loading plan.

Do you handle antiques?

We can help with many antique and sentimental household pieces. Extremely high-value or museum-level items may require specialty crating or separate insurance arrangements.

Can you help with storage?

Yes. We can help prepare, label, move, and organize fragile items for storage when the job requires careful placement and access planning.

Do you move mirrors and glass tops?

Yes. Mirrors and glass pieces require careful protection, upright handling when appropriate, and clear labeling.

What areas do you serve?

We serve Westchester County, New York City, New Jersey, Connecticut, and surrounding local moving routes.
